entry.description: OpenAI Math family 110, Optimal-order randomized k-server on arbitrary metrics. OpenAI's 6 October 2026 catalogue reports: Establishes a randomized competitive ratio O(\log^2(k+1)) for k-server on every metric space, matching the worst-case lower-bound order. One policy serves every finite oblivious request sequence, including on infinite unbounded metrics. On finite rational metrics, a uniform implementation has polynomial preprocessing and per-request bit cost in the input length and \log(t+1) at request t, with a finite instance-dependent additive movement constant. entry.description: OpenAI Math family 115, Sampling and counting contingency tables with arbitrary margins. OpenAI's 6 October 2026 catalogue reports: For nonnegative integer matrices with prescribed row and column sums, gives exact uniform sampling in expected polynomial bit time and almost-uniform sampling in worst-case polynomial bit time. The dimensions and binary-encoded margins are unrestricted. Also gives a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for counting such tables with arbitrary individual cell bounds, including structural zeros, with polynomial cost on every execution. OpenAI says an internal frontier model produced the released result package; its repository warns that results have different verification statuses and that some unformalized results could have issues. OpenAI links a Lean companion for the family, but this run did not replay it or establish statement correspondence. This source-attributed record remains provisional=1. Further checking: Independently review OpenAI family 115 (Sampling and counting contingency tables with arbitrary margins) for correctness, novelty, priority, imported hypotheses, and exact claim scope. A family-level Lean document is linked, but its scope and statement correspondence have not been independently checked. Reconcile the catalogue summary with all 2 constituent manuscripts; reconstruct family-specific human/model generation, checking, and write-up roles; and monitor OpenAI's promised versioned corrections. The repository-level production statement and catalogue grouping do not by themselves establish correctness, novelty, family-level attribution, or end-to-end verification. No downloaded proof, code, certificate, macro, PDF, or Lean artifact was executed or independently replayed in this run.
